冶.meaning: A tiny blacksmith mouse sets a thimble of tin on a stone <part>pedestal</part> over her candle and watches it glow and run like honey. Then she pours it into a mould packed in <part>ice</part>, where it hisses into a tiny sword. Her favourite part is the <kanji>melting</kanji>.
冶.on: She wraps the warm hilt in a scrap of <sound>ya</sound>rn so she can hold it.
冶.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' she squeaks when a hot drop splashes her tail, and carries on casting.

沃.meaning: A garden gnome in a <part>tilted hat</part> catches <part>water drops</part> in its brim every night and tips them onto the soil at dawn. Soon its patch grows pumpkins the size of cars and carrots taller than the shed. No soil in town can match its <kanji>fertility</kanji>.
沃.on: One morning a <sound>yo</sound>-yo dropped in the patch sprouts into a whole yo-yo bush.
沃.kun: So the neighbours pour water over an old <sound>so</sound>fa and a lost <sound>so</sound>ck on the lawn, hoping they sprout too.

苛.meaning: A gardener trims her <part>grass</part> blade by blade with nail scissors, desperate for the show judge's <part>approval</part>. Every year he squints and says, 'One blade is crooked.' Every year she trims again. Ten years of that one crooked blade: pure <kanji>torment</kanji>.
苛.on: She shows him her pond, hoping a big orange <sound>ca</sound>rp will cheer him up. It splashes his clipboard.
苛.kun: '<sound>Ea</sound>sy!' he tells her, then drives off in his <sound>jee</sound>p, right across her lawn: what a bully.

采.meaning: Under an old <part>tree</part>, a raccoon runs a midnight game. With one <part>claw</part> it scoops up two little cubes, shakes them and rolls them across a root. The squirrels gasp: double six again. Nobody ever beats the raccoon's lucky <kanji>dice</kanji>.
采.on: The winner gets a jug of apple <sound>ci</sound>der, and it's always the raccoon.
采.kun: Then it takes all the acorns and stacks them behind a <sound>to</sound>tem pole.

咽.meaning: An opera hippo opens her huge <part>mouth</part> for the high note, and nothing comes out but a squeak. The doctor peers in with a torch and finds the <part>cause</part>: a ping-pong ball stuck halfway down her <kanji>throat</kanji>.
咽.on: He fishes it out stained blue: she had gargled <sound>in</sound>k by mistake.
咽.kun: In the front row, a <sound>moo</sound>se laughs so hard it chokes and splutters all over the <sound>se</sound>at in front.

剝.meaning: A sticker of a smiling sun has been stuck on the town <part>fountain</part> for years. The caretaker warms it with an <part>iron</part>, slides a blunt little <part>dagger</part> under one corner and pulls. With a long, happy rip, the whole sticker starts to <kanji>come off</kanji>.
剝.on: Underneath, someone long ago painted a purple <sound>huck</sound>leberry.
剝.kun: A <sound>he</sound>n hops up and pecks away the last flakes of glue: stripped clean.

朕.meaning: An <part>alien</part> lands on the <part>moon</part>, plants a flag and crowns himself king of all the craters. From then on he never says 'I': 'We are hungry', 'We shall nap now', though he's the only one there. He speaks in the <kanji>imperial we</kanji>.
朕.on: He strokes his long green <sound>chin</sound> and announces, 'We approve.'

淫.meaning: A sailor's parrot perches on a <part>spindle</part> by the dock, dipping one <part>claw</part> in the <part>water drops</part>, and screeches rude rhymes at every passing boat. The vicar covers his ears and the ladies row faster. That bird is the harbour's one source of <kanji>lewdness</kanji>.
淫.on: The vicar blacks out the rhymes it reads off the dock wall with a pot of <sound>in</sound>k.
淫.kun: '<sound>Hee</sound>-hee,' cackles the parrot, as the vicar soaks his brush in a <sound>tu</sound>b of soapy water: to soak.

羞.meaning: A <part>sheep</part> sneaks into the barn, grabs a <part>C-clamp</part> and tries to fix the fence it broke. One wild <part>slash</part> of the clamp, and the whole fence falls flat just as the farmer walks in. The sheep hides its face in its wool: it can only <kanji>feel ashamed</kanji>.
羞.on: It tries to hide behind the farmer's giant muddy <sound>shoe</sound>.
羞.kun: <sound>Hu</sound>mbled, it climbs into the farmer's <sound>jee</sound>p and hides under a sack.

舷.meaning: A cat crosses the harbour by walking the top edge of a rowing <part>boat</part> like a tightrope, while a fisherman reels in his line on a squeaky <part>spool</part>. Each time the boat rocks, the cat grips that narrow wooden rim tighter: the <kanji>gunwale</kanji>.
舷.on: 'Steady, <sound>Gen</sound>!' the fisherman calls to the cat, whose name is Gen.
舷.kun: The fisherman's <sound>foo</sound>t knocks a bag of <sound>nu</sound>ts and a <sound>bu</sound>tter <sound>tu</sound>b along the rim.

僅.meaning: A giant hangs his coat on a <part>coat hook</part> nailed to a hill and sits down to a feast. He opens his huge <part>mouth</part>, but his plate holds just one blade of <part>grass</part> and one crumb of <part>soil</part>. It's hard to fill a giant with a meal so <kanji>slight</kanji>.
僅.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher drops him a minnow, which doesn't help much.
僅.kun: He stares in <sound>wo</sound>nder at dessert: one drop of yu<sound>zu</sound> juice.

塡.meaning: A dog digs forty holes in the lawn before its owner gets home. In a panic it grabs a <part>spoon</part> and every garden <part>tool</part> it can drag, and shovels the <part>soil</part> back as fast as its paws allow. When the door opens, it sits wagging, having raced to <kanji>fill in</kanji> every last hole.
塡.on: Next door, a <sound>ten</sound>or leans out of the window and sings it a victory song.
塡.kun: <sound>Hu</sound>ffing, it pushes its nose into the last <sound>mu</sound>d hole, and it fits perfectly: stuck tight.

慄.meaning: A cowboy camps under a lone <part>tree</part> out <part>west</part>. At midnight the branches creak and whisper, his <part>heartbeat</part> drums in his ears and his teeth chatter. In the morning it turns out to be a goat chewing the bark, but it was a long night's <kanji>shiver</kanji>.
慄.on: He calms his nerves by nibbling a whole box of <sound>Ritz</sound> crackers.
慄.kun: He trembles under his <sound>fu</sound>ton while a <sound>roo</sound>k laughs at him from the branch.

虞.meaning: At the zoo gift shop, a <part>tiger</part> in a bow tie holds out a box and purrs, 'I <part>give</part> this to you.' The box is ticking. Your hand hovers over it: a gift, or a trick? You reach out slowly, full of <kanji>apprehension</kanji>.
虞.on: Inside is only a small <sound>goo</sound>die bag, rattling with sweets.
虞.kun: You tip it out: a jelly <sound>o</sound>ctopus, a tiny <sound>so</sound>fa and a <sound>re</sound>d note that says 'BOO'.

詣.meaning: A snail sets off when the town announces a picnic, crawling for a whole year towards the smell of something <part>delicious</part>. It reaches the park just as the mayor ends his closing <part>speech</part> and everyone is packing up. Still, the snail is proud: it did <kanji>arrive</kanji>.
詣.on: One slice of <sound>ca</sound>ke has been saved, just for it.
詣.kun: The snail bows to the mayor, its shell trailing behind like a royal <sound>ca</sound>pe: a polite visit.
